==English== {{wp|}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=desire|:inh|enm:wanten|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|wanten||to lack, to need}}, from {{der|en|non|vanta||to lack}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wanatōną||to be wanting, lack}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*wanô||lack, deficiency}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁weh₂-||empty}}. Cognate with {{cog|gmh|wan||not full, empty}}, {{cog|dum|wan||empty, poor}}, {{cog|ang|wana||want, lack, absence, deficiency}}, {{cog|la|vanus||empty}}. See {{l|en|wan}}, {{l|en|wan-}}. {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₁weh₂-}} ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|en|waunt||obsolete}} ====Pronunciation==== * {{homophones|en|wa'n't}} * {{enPR|wŏnt|wŭnt|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/wɒnt/}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-to want.ogg|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-want.wav|a=Southern England}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Nattes à chat-want.wav}} * {{enPR|wŏnt|wŭnt|wônt|a=GA}} {{IPA|en|/wɑnt/|/wʌnt/|/wɔnt/}}[http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/want Dictionary.com] ** {{audio|en|en-us-want.ogg|a=California}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-wont.ogg|a=California}} * {{IPA|en|[wɔːnt]|[wʌnt]|a=CA}} * {{enPR|wŏnt|a=Aus}}, {{IPA|en|/wɔnt/}} * {{enPR|wŏnt|wŭnt|a=NZ}}, {{IPA|en|/wɒnt/|/wɐnt/|q2=nonstandard}} * {{IPA|en|/ʋɔɳʈ/|/ʋɑɳʈ/|a=Indic}} ** {{hmp|en|vaunt}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒnt|ʌnt|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[wish]] for or [[desire]] (something); to feel a [[need]] or desire for; to [[crave]], [[hanker]], or [[demand]]. {{defdate|from 18th c.}} #: {{ux|en|I '''want''' you as a friend, not a foe.}} #: {{ux|en|What do you '''want''' to eat?  I '''want''' you to leave.  I never '''wanted''' to go back to live with my mother.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=13|passage=And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He spoke with extreme contempt of the dense stupidity exhibited on all occasions by the working classes. He said that if you '''wanted''' to do anything for them, you must rule them, not pamper them. Soft heartedness caused more harm than good.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=July-August|author=w:Henry Petroski |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/4/geothermal-energy Geothermal Energy] |volume=101|issue=4|magazine=w:American Scientist |passage=Energy has seldom been found where we need it when we '''want''' it. Ancient nomads, wishing to ward off the evening chill and enjoy a meal around a campfire, had to collect wood and then spend time and effort coaxing the heat of friction out from between sticks to kindle a flame. With more settled people, animals were harnessed to capstans or caged in treadmills to turn grist into meal.}} #*: I '''want''' to find a supermarket. — Oh, okay. The supermarket is at 1500 Irving Street. It is near the apartment. — Great! ## {{lb|en|by extension}} To make it easy or tempting to do something undesirable, or to make it hard or challenging to refrain from doing it. ##: {{ux|en|The game developers of Candy Crush '''want''' you to waste large, copious amounts of your money on in-game purchases to buy boosters and lives.}} ##: {{ux|en|Depression '''wants''' you to feel like the world is dark and that you are not worthy of happiness. The first step to making your life better from this day forward is to stop believing these lies.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|in particular}} To [[wish]], [[desire]]{{,}} or [[demand]] to [[see]], have the [[presence]] of or do business with. #: {{ux|en|Ma’am, you are exactly the professional we '''want''' for this job.}} #: {{ux|en|Danish police '''want''' him for embezzlement.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Fred Vargas|title=The Chalk Circle Man|publisher=Vintage Canada|isbn=9780307374035|page=75 |passage=But now it's different, if the police '''want''' him for murder.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[desire#Verb|desire]] (to experience [[desire#Noun|desire]]); to wish. #: {{ux|en|You can leave if you '''want'''.}} #* '''2019''' May 5, "{{w|The Last of the Starks}}", ''Game of Thrones'' season 8 episode 4 (written by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss): # {{lb|en|colloquial|usually second person or interrogative|often future tense}} To be advised to do or aim for something {{q|compare {{m|en|should}}, {{m|en|ought}}}}. #: {{ux|en|You’ll '''want''' to repeat this three or four times to get the best result.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|now|colloquial}} To lack and be in need of or [[require]] (something, such as a noun or verbal noun). {{defdate|from 15th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1741|title=The Gentleman's and London Magazine: Or Monthly Chronologer, 1741-1794|page=559 |passage=The lady, it is said, will inherit a fortune of three hundred pounds a year, with two cool thousands left by an uncle, on her arriving at the age of twenty-one, of which she '''wants''' but a few months.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1839|title=Chambers's Journal|page=123 |passage=Oh Jeanie, it will be hard, after every thing is ready for our happiness, if we should be sundered. It '''wants''' but a few days o' Martinmas, and then I maun enter on my new service on Loch Rannoch, where a bonny shieling is ready ...}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1847|title=The American Protestant|page=27 |passage=In this we have just read an address to children in England, Ireland, and Scotland, in behalf of children who '''want''' food to keep them from starvation.}} #* {{RQ:Carroll Alice|page=96|passage=“Your hair '''wants''' cutting,” said the Hatter. He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity, and this was his first speech.}} #* {{RQ:Woolf Jacob's Room|chapter=II|page=22|passage=The mowing-machine always '''wanted''' oiling. Barnet turned it under Jacob's window, and it creaked—creaked, and rattled across the lawn and creaked again.}} #: {{ux|en|That chair '''wants''' fixing and a clean.}} #: {{ux|en|What you really '''want''' is a good smack!}} # {{lb|en|transitive|now|rare}} To have occasion for (something requisite or useful); to require or need. #* {{RQ:Young Night-Thoughts|passage=Man '''wants''' but little, nor that little long.}} #* {{RQ:Goldsmith Vicar of Wakefield|passage=Man '''wants''' but little here below, nor '''wants''' that little long.}} #* {{RQ:Thoreau Walden|passage=[F]or my greatest skill has been to '''want''' but little.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|dated}} To be [[lacking]] or [[deficient]] or [[absent]]. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #: {{ux|en|There was something '''wanting''' in the play.}} #* {{RQ:Purchas Pilgrimes|page=404|passage=They of the Citie fought valiantly with Engines, Darts, Arrows: and when Stones '''wanted''', they threw Silver, especially molten silver.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Miscellaneous Works|chapter=Preface|passage=The disposition, the manners, and the thoughts are all before it; where any of those are '''wanting''' or imperfect, so much '''wants''' or is imperfect in the imitation of human life.}} #* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Criticism|passage=For as in bodies, thus in souls, we find / What '''wants''' in blood and spirits, swelled with wind.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|dated}} To be in a state of destitution; to be needy; to lack. #* {{RQ:Jonson Volpone|passage=You have a gift, sir (thank your education), / Will never let you '''want'''.}} #: {{ux|en|The paupers desperately '''want'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[lack]] and be without, to not have (something). {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #* {{RQ:Burton Melancholy|edition=2nd|partition=2|section=3|member=7|passage=he that hath skill to be a pilot '''wants''' a ship; and he that could govern a commonwealth{{...}}'''wants''' means to exercise his worth, hath not a poor office to manage.}} #* {{RQ:Spectator|issue=108|date=4 July 1711|passage=I observed {{...}} that your whip '''wanted''' a lash to it.}} #* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver's Travels|page=141|passage=The least miserable among them appear to be those who turn to Dotage, and entirely lose their Memories; these meet with more Pity and Assistance, because they '''want''' many bad Qualities which abound in others.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1765|author=w:James Merrick|title=Psalams |passage=Not what we wish, but what we '''want''', / Oh, let thy grace supply!}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1981|author=w:A. D. Hope|chapter=His Coy Mistress to Mr. Marvell|chapterurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716071607/https://www.poetrylibrary.edu.au/poets/hope-a-d/poems/v-andrew-marvell-and-his-coy-mistress-0143005|title=A Book of Answers |passage=Pray Mr Marvell, can it be / You think to have persuaded me? / Then let me say: you '''want''' the art / To woo, much less to win my heart.}} #: {{ux|en|She '''wanted''' anything she needed.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete|by extension}} To [[lack]] and perhaps be able or willing to [[do without]]. #* {{RQ:Purchas Pilgrimes|page=50|passage={{...}} which the Kings of Assyria had left for the maintenance of this Temple sacrifices, after the ouerthrow thereof, was shared among the Chaldzans; which they by this attempt were like to lose, and therefore were willing to '''want''' his presence.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1797|journal=The European Magazine, and London Review|page=226 |passage=For Law, Physick and Divinitie, need so the help of tongs and sciences, as thei can not '''want''' them, and yet thei require so a hole mans studie, as thei may parte with no tyme to other lerning, ...}} #*: "Are ye [[sharp-set]]?" he asked, glancing at about the level of my knee. "Ye can eat that drop [[parritch]]."
I said I feared it was his own supper.
"Oh," said he, "I can do fine '''wanting''' it, I'll take the ale, though, for it [[slocken]]s my cough." He drank the cup about half out, still keeping an eye upon me as he drank... # To [[desire]] a [[romantic]] or {{lb|en|especially}} [[sexual]] [[relationship]] with someone; to [[lust]] for. #: {{ux|en|Dang, girl! Your brother is gorgeous! I '''want''' him so bad!}} #* {{quote-song|en|author={{w|Jo Callis}}; {{w|Philip Oakey}}; {{w|Philip Adrian Wright}}|authorlabel=no|title={{w|Don't You Want Me|Don't You '''Want''' Me}}|album={{w|Dare (album)|Dare}}|date=27 November 1981|artist={{w|The Human League}}|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uPudE8nDog0|text=Don't, don't you '''want''' me? / You know I can't believe it when I hear that you won't see me / Don't, don't you '''want''' me? / You know I don't believe you when you say that you don't need me}} #* {{quote-song|en|author={{w|Tate McRae}}; {{w|Amy Allen (songwriter)|Amy Allen}}; Jasper Harris; {{w|Ryan Tedder}}|authorlabel=no|title={{w|Greedy (Tate McRae song)|Greedy}}|album={{w|Think Later}}|date=15 September 2023|artist={{w|Tate McRae}}|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8AtiHCDGZ8c|text=Yeah, you're loo- (loo-loo-) lookin' at me like I'm some sweet escape / Obvious that you '''want''' me, but I said...}} =====Usage notes===== * This is a [[catenative]] verb.
